# speed

> speed is a modular monolith distributed as libraries: independently released Go
> modules and npm packages that business projects pull in via `go get` / `npm install`
> and compile into one binary, with multi-tenant isolation, authentication and
> permissions, organizations, subscription billing and metering, an AI gateway,
> background jobs, media storage, notifications, observability and an operations
> console already built in. It is not an application you run and not a repository you
> fork. Nothing is published to a registry yet — the whole tree is a real, buildable
> checkout, not a pre-release preview.

The documentation is organized in two main sections — User guides (for teams using
speed modules in their own product) and Developer docs (for developers working on
speed itself) — plus the site-level pages for AI agents and about. Pages below
are English; every page has a Chinese (zh-cn) translation under the identical path
with a `/zh-cn/` prefix, listed once here rather than duplicated per language.

## Start here

- [For AI Agents](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/ai-agents/): what to read first as a coding agent, the architecture
  rules that most often matter (module dependency direction, API-contract spec-first
  order, the four data domains, deployment mode vs. implementation composition).
- [Root AGENTS.md](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/AGENTS.md): the repository's own first-read orientation
  for any AI coding tool.
## User guides (using speed in your product)

- [User guides](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/user-guide/): section index — the overall introduction, the
  domain-by-domain fast starts, and the complete per-module usage reference.
- [Domain guides](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/user-guide/domains/): eight fast-start pages, one per product
  domain (identity and access, tenancy and organizations, data and configuration, billing
  and metering, jobs and notifications, storage sharing and AI, observability and
  operations, building the frontend), each with minimal integration steps and an example.
- [Quickstart](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/user-guide/quickstart/): generate a starter project with `saasctl new`, the
  four `saasctl` commands (`new`, `upgrade`, `db migrate`, `config print`), and how to
  run Go commands in this repository's workspace layout.
- [Module reference](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/user-guide/modules/): one usage page per Go module and npm package
  (21 + 12), grouped by dependency layer — what it is for, when to choose it, how to wire
  it, runnable examples, known limitations.
- [API reference](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/user-guide/api-reference/): the complete platform HTTP API, rendered
  from the merged OpenAPI contract of the eleven platform modules — every operation,
  parameter, schema and error (interactive).
- [Configuration reference](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/user-guide/configuration/): every configuration value a
  speed-based application resolves — the process-start bootstrap keys platform modules
  declare (each with the environment variable name the loader derives for its key
  path), the loader mechanism a host drives to resolve them, plus the dynamic
  configuration items and feature flags an operator edits per tenant.
- [Error code index](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/user-guide/error-codes/): every structured error code a speed-based API
  can answer with — HTTP status, locale message, triggering condition and source,
  grouped by module.

## Developer docs (developing speed itself)

- [Developer docs](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/developer-docs/): section index — architecture, design principles,
  per-module design deep dives explaining the rationale behind each module's shape,
  API-contract and release mechanics, and contributing guidance.
- [Module design](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/developer-docs/modules/): one design page per Go module and npm package
  (21 + 12): responsibility and boundary, design rationale and trade-offs, key
  mechanisms, frozen public API — with mermaid diagrams.
- [Architecture](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/developer-docs/architecture/): the modular monolith, module dependency
  direction, the deployment mode / implementation composition axes, and the wiring
  contract.
- [Design principles](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/developer-docs/design-principles/): the discipline every module obeys and
  why, with where each rule is enforced.
## Site pages

- [Home](https://speed.vislake.com/): landing page and site map.
- [Documentation](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/): the section hub linking both main sections.
- [About](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/about/): what speed is, how the pieces fit together, how its
  documentation is distributed.
- [For AI Agents](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/ai-agents/): what to read first as a coding agent (also listed under
  Start here above).
- [Design decisions](https://speed.vislake.com/docs/developer-docs/design-decisions/): the repository's ADR record,
  surfaced.

## Module documentation (go/ — repository assets, per-module discipline)

- [pkgcore](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/pkgcore/AGENTS.md): the
  dependency floor — Module/Registry/Kernel wiring, seam registries, the merged i18n
  catalog.
- [dbkit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/dbkit/AGENTS.md): dual-dialect
  `*gorm.DB` wrapper, the mandatory generic Repository[T], migrations, field encryption,
  blind indexing, soft/hard delete.
- [tenancy](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/tenancy/AGENTS.md): tenant
  resolution, the audited system-context escape hatch, isolation test suites.
- [observability](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/observability/AGENTS.md):
  OpenTelemetry init, redacted structured logging, HTTP metrics middleware.
- [config](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/config/AGENTS.md): dynamic,
  scoped configuration with encrypted sensitive items and pre-auth endpoints.
- [jobs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/jobs/AGENTS.md): the background
  job queue contract, standalone (SQLite) and distributed (Redis) implementations.
- [ratelimit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/ratelimit/AGENTS.md): a
  KVStore-backed rate limiter shared across modules.
- [pki](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/pki/AGENTS.md): signing-key and
  X.509 certificate lifecycle management.
- [authn](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/authn/AGENTS.md):
  authentication — passwords, sessions, MFA, social/enterprise sign-in.
- [rbac](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/rbac/AGENTS.md): role-based
  access control, deny-by-default, no dependency on authn.
- [org](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/org/AGENTS.md): a tenant's
  organization tree, memberships and invitations.
- [storage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/storage/AGENTS.md): tenant
  object storage lifecycle over the ObjectStore seam.
- [notification](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/notification/AGENTS.md):
  the platform's messaging surface — type registry, inbox, consent-verified delivery.
- [billing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/billing/AGENTS.md): plans,
  entitlements, subscriptions, credits ledger, real payment gateways.
- [metering](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/metering/AGENTS.md): usage
  recording with analytics-grade and billing-grade reliability tiers.
- [sharing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/sharing/AGENTS.md): public
  share links with forced expiry, instant revocation and access logging.
- [integration](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/integration/AGENTS.md): a
  tenant's outward-facing API surface — API keys and outbound webhooks.
- [ai-gateway](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/ai-gateway/AGENTS.md): a
  vendor-agnostic LLM chat and image-generation gateway.
- [compliance](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/compliance/AGENTS.md):
  retention sweeps, right-to-erasure, export delivery, audit querying.
- [admin](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/admin/AGENTS.md): the
  operations-console backend — tenant ledger, impersonation, cross-tenant search.
- [saasctl](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/go/saasctl/AGENTS.md): the
  consumer-facing CLI (`new`, `upgrade`, `db migrate`, `config print`).

## Package documentation (web/packages/ — repository assets)

- [tokens](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/tokens/AGENTS.md):
  the design-token tree as dependency-free pure data.
- [i18n](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/i18n/AGENTS.md): the
  react-i18next wrapper mirroring pkgcore's message catalog.
- [ui-kit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/ui-kit/AGENTS.md):
  the MUI v9 theme factory and seven controlled components.
- [api-client](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/api-client/AGENTS.md):
  the single hand-written HTTP client home — token store, retry, refresh.
- [api-sdk](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/api-sdk/AGENTS.md):
  the generated typed surface of the merged OpenAPI document.
- [layout-kit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/layout-kit/AGENTS.md):
  shared app chrome — AppShell and RouteGuard.
- [auth-core](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/auth-core/AGENTS.md):
  the headless session state machine over the generated authn surface.
- [auth-ui](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/auth-ui/AGENTS.md):
  the sign-in component family.
- [tenancy-ui](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/tenancy-ui/AGENTS.md):
  the controlled TenantSwitcher component.
- [product-shell](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/product-shell/AGENTS.md):
  the tenant-facing assembly shell.
- [account-ui](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/account-ui/AGENTS.md):
  the signed-in account-management component family.
- [billing-ui](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vislake/speed/main/web/packages/billing-ui/AGENTS.md):
  the billing-documents read surface over the generated billing operations.

## Reference application (mandatory first consumer of every module)

- [Reference app](https://github.com/vislake/speed/tree/main/examples/reference-app): the AI
  smile-simulation dental SaaS that exercises every module, and its own web host
  composing every `@speed/*` package together.

  the row-for-row JSON twin of the site's error-code index (the site page above is the
  human-readable form).
